WPG generates 2.9 expected goals per 60 and allows 3.3. CHI sits at 2.6 for and 3.61 against, so its defense has been the bigger leak, and the 4.14 goals per game it has given up bears that out. On special teams, WPG's power play is creating 0.66 expected goals per game to CHI's 0.32, while WPG's penalty kill allows 0.58 to CHI's 0.44. The model has WPG at 3.04 expected goals tonight and CHI at 2.82.

In net, projected starter Stuart Skinner (WPG) is at +3.44 goals saved above expected over four games, with +5.96 across 50 games last season. Projected CHI starter Spencer Knight is at -0.34 this season with a .885 save percentage, but he was +11.11 across 55 games last year, so the gap may be more about early-season noise than a lasting split.

Recent form is closer than the records suggest. WPG is 4-1-0 in its last five but has won the chance battle in only two of them, averaging 46% of the expected goals. CHI is 2-3-0 with the same 46% average, having out-chanced an opponent once. For the player picks, the model likes Kyle Connor most, at 43% to score and 30% for two or more points. For CHI, Connor Bedard is the top pick at 33% to score and 28% for two or more points.
